a1_answer:
NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a duty-cycle modulation of the steam blow-through valve during grade changes to prevent condensate accumulation. Standard practice uses continuous blow-through or fixed scheduling; the mitigation is a dynamically scheduled blow-through synchronized with the condensate surge, triggered by steam pressure drop. This attacks the driving mechanism of water hammer by ensuring steam flow velocity remains above the critical threshold for condensate plug formation. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest practice is fixed-interval blow-down scheduling; this is different because it uses real-time steam pressure as a feedback signal to time blow-through exactly when condensate accumulation begins, not on a fixed timer. The mechanism is a closed-loop duty cycle on the blow-through valve, modulated by steam pressure drop.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the Froude number for stratified flow: Fr = v / √(g·D), where v is steam velocity, g is gravity, and D is pipe diameter. Water hammer occurs when Fr < 1 (stratified to slug flow transition). The intervention increases v by opening the blow-through valve during pressure drops, raising Fr above 1. A 20% steam pressure drop (typical in grade changes) would reduce v by ~20%; the blow-through increases v by 30%, netting a 10% increase in Fr, preventing the transition.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
- (a) Existing steam pressure transducer at dryer section inlet (signal source)
- (a) Existing blow-through control valve (actuator)
- (c) Control logic modification: Set blow-through valve to open when steam pressure drops >15% for >10 sec (parameter change)
- (c) Schedule: Blow-through duty cycle = 30 sec open / 90 sec closed during grade changes (parameter change)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice uses continuous blow-through (constant steam loss). This intervention replaces continuous blow-through with a pulsed schedule, reducing steam consumption by 60% (operational cost: 0.6× continuous steam loss). Installation burden: Zero (uses existing control system). Commissioning burden: 2 (logic programming, same as standard practice tuning). Maintenance burden: Same (valve wear unchanged). Net burden: Lower due to steam savings.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install calibrated pressure transducers; monitor steam pressure and valve position during grade changes. Instruments: Existing pressure transducer, data logger. Pass/fail: Water hammer events must decrease by >50% over 10 grade changes. Duration: 1 week. Kill criterion: If water hammer rate does not decrease, revert to continuous blow-through.
